summary: Validation library exposes require and module on globalThis
details: On require/import of the main entrypoint, runtimekit executes `global.r = require` and `global.m = module` (lib/index.cjs and lib/index.mjs around line 638), publishing the host's `require` function and the module object onto the Node global namespace under single-letter aliases. The package advertises itself as a TypeScript runtime-validation library (a clone of the `runtypes` API surface) and there is no documented reason for this side effect. The assignment alone does not exfiltrate data, fetch external code, or execute a payload, so it is not in itself an active attack or install-time RCE. However, it is a backdoor-staging primitive: any other code subsequently loaded in the same process — including code reached via an eval/prototype-pollution sink — gains a clean handle to `require('child_process')` and to walk `module.parent`/`module.children` for the host module graph. The pattern has no legitimate purpose for a validation library and warrants human review to decide whether a public advisory is appropriate.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
